fr.title: Conheça a obra: IKEA Instructions
s: IKEA, the Swedish furniture company founded by Ingvar Kamprad in 1943, began to sell flat-pack furniture in 1956, so customers carry the pieces home and assemble them.
A IKEA, empresa sueca de móveis fundada por Ingvar Kamprad em 1943, começou a vender móveis desmontados em 1956, para que os clientes levem as peças para casa e as montem.
The instructions have almost no words, only drawings, because they are made for people of all languages.
As instruções quase não têm palavras, só desenhos, porque são feitas para pessoas de todas as línguas.
In written instructions, the passive voice is very common: “The screws are inserted. The panel is attached.”
Em instruções escritas, a voz passiva é muito comum: “The screws are inserted. The panel is attached.”
Use “is/are + past participle” for each step: “The bolts are tightened.”
Use “is/are + particípio” para cada etapa: “The bolts are tightened.”
A warning can also be passive: “The product must be unplugged before cleaning.”
Um aviso também pode ser passivo: “The product must be unplugged before cleaning.”
Batteries are not included.
Pilhas não estão incluídas.
Read the instructions before you start.
Leia as instruções antes de começar.

fr.title: Conheça a obra: Chinese Whispers
s: “Chinese Whispers” is a children's game, called “telephone” in the United States, in which a message is whispered from person to person.
“Chinese Whispers” é um jogo infantil, chamado de “telephone” nos Estados Unidos, em que uma mensagem é sussurrada de pessoa em pessoa.
By the end, the message is usually very different from the first one, which makes everyone laugh.
No final, a mensagem geralmente é muito diferente da primeira, o que faz todos rirem.
The game is a perfect example of reported speech, because we pass on what others said.
O jogo é um exemplo perfeito de discurso indireto, porque repassamos o que outros disseram.
“She said she was hungry.” “He said he had seen a lion.”
“She said she was hungry.” “He said he had seen a lion.”
Remember the change: “am” becomes “was”, “will” becomes “would”, “have seen” becomes “had seen”.
Lembre da mudança: “am” vira “was”, “will” vira “would”, “have seen” vira “had seen”.
Place and time words change too: “here” becomes “there”, “today” becomes “that day”.
Palavras de lugar e tempo também mudam: “here” vira “there”, “today” vira “that day”.
Listen carefully before you pass it on.
Escute com atenção antes de passar adiante.

s: “The Call of the Wild” is a novel by the American writer Jack London, published in 1903.
“O Chamado da Selva” é um romance do escritor americano Jack London, publicado em 1903.
Buck, a strong dog, is stolen from a comfortable home in California and sold as a sled dog in the Yukon during the Gold Rush.
Buck, um cão forte, é roubado de uma casa confortável na Califórnia e vendido como cão de trenó no Yukon durante a corrida do ouro.
He works day and night in the snow, and little by little he returns to his wild instincts.
Ele trabalha dia e noite na neve e, aos poucos, volta aos seus instintos selvagens.
When someone works late at night, we say they “burn the midnight oil”: “I'm burning the midnight oil to finish the report.”
Quando alguém trabalha até tarde da noite, dizemos que “burn the midnight oil”: “I'm burning the midnight oil to finish the report.”
“Work around the clock” means to work all day and night.
“Work around the clock” significa trabalhar dia e noite.
“Hard at work” and “keep your nose to the grindstone” also describe effort.
“Hard at work” e “keep your nose to the grindstone” também descrevem esforço.
Take a break, because too much work is bad for you.
Faça uma pausa, porque trabalho demais faz mal.

s: “All the President's Men” is a 1976 film about the Watergate scandal, based on the book by the journalists Bob Woodward and Carl Bernstein.
“Todos os Homens do Presidente” é um filme de 1976 sobre o escândalo Watergate, baseado no livro dos jornalistas Bob Woodward e Carl Bernstein.
The two reporters discover that men connected to the White House organized a break-in, and the story leads to the resignation of President Nixon in 1974.
Os dois repórteres descobrem que homens ligados à Casa Branca organizaram um arrombamento, e a história leva à renúncia do presidente Nixon em 1974.
In the film, many people admit, deny or refuse to talk.
No filme, muitas pessoas admitem, negam ou se recusam a falar.
Reporting verbs give more information than “said”: “He admitted that he knew. She denied that she was there.”
Verbos de relato dão mais informação do que “said”: “He admitted that he knew. She denied that she was there.”
Use “suggested”, “promised”, “warned” and “refused” in the same way: “He refused to answer.”
Use “suggested”, “promised”, “warned” e “refused” da mesma forma: “He refused to answer.”
Some verbs take “to + verb” (promise, refuse), others take “that” or -ing (admit, suggest).
Alguns verbos pedem “to + verbo” (promise, refuse), outros pedem “that” ou -ing (admit, suggest).
Follow the facts, not the rumors.
Siga os fatos, não os boatos.

fr.title: Conheça a obra: The Telephone Call
s: “A Telephone Call” is a short story by Dorothy Parker, published in 1928, in which a woman waits desperately for a man to call.
“A Telephone Call” é um conto de Dorothy Parker, publicado em 1928, em que uma mulher espera desesperadamente que um homem ligue.
The whole story is her thoughts, and she begs God to make the phone ring.
A história inteira são os pensamentos dela, e ela implora a Deus que faça o telefone tocar.
In real life, a phone call often ends with a message left for someone else.
Na vida real, uma ligação muitas vezes termina com um recado deixado para outra pessoa.
To take a message, say “Can I take a message?” and to leave one, say “Could you tell him that I called?”
Para anotar um recado, diga “Can I take a message?” e para deixar um, diga “Could you tell him that I called?”
To pass it on: “She asked me to tell you that it's urgent.”
Para repassar: “She asked me to tell you that it's urgent.”
Ask for a callback: “Please ask her to call me back.”
Peça um retorno: “Please ask her to call me back.”
The line may be busy, so be available.
A linha pode estar ocupada, então fique disponível.

fr.title: Conheça a obra: Ghost
s: “Ghost” is a 1990 romantic fantasy film with Patrick Swayze, Demi Moore and Whoopi Goldberg.
“Ghost” (Ghost: Do Outro Lado da Vida) é um filme de fantasia romântica de 1990 com Patrick Swayze, Demi Moore e Whoopi Goldberg.
Sam is killed, but his spirit stays on Earth and uses a medium, Oda Mae, to pass messages to his girlfriend, Molly.
Sam é assassinado, mas seu espírito fica na Terra e usa uma médium, Oda Mae, para passar recados à namorada, Molly.
Oda Mae always begins with, “He says that…”
Oda Mae sempre começa com “He says that…”
To pass on a message, use “tell” and “ask”: “He told me to tell you that he loves you. He asked me to say that he is here.”
Para passar um recado, use “tell” e “ask”: “He told me to tell you that he loves you. He asked me to say that he is here.”
With orders, use “tell someone to do”: “He told me to hurry.”
Com ordens, use “tell someone to do”: “He told me to hurry.”
With requests, use “ask someone to do”: “She asked me to wait.”
Com pedidos, use “ask someone to do”: “She asked me to wait.”
Messages travel between worlds.
Recados viajam entre mundos.

fr.title: Conheça a obra: Whisper Down the Lane
s: “Whisper Down the Lane” is the American name of the game called “Chinese Whispers” in Britain.
“Whisper Down the Lane” é o nome americano do jogo chamado “Chinese Whispers” na Grã-Bretanha.
One child whispers a sentence to the next, and by the end it has changed.
Uma criança sussurra uma frase para a próxima, e no final ela mudou.
In a noisy place, it is easy to hear something wrong, so you have to ask for clarification.
Num lugar barulhento, é fácil ouvir errado, então você precisa pedir esclarecimento.
To ask someone to repeat, say “Sorry, what did you say?” or “Could you repeat that?”
Para pedir que alguém repita, diga “Sorry, what did you say?” ou “Could you repeat that?”
To check, say “Did you say the bus?” or “Do you mean the radio?”
Para confirmar, diga “Did you say the bus?” ou “Do you mean the radio?”
Speak more slowly in noisy places.
Fale mais devagar em lugares barulhentos.
Never be afraid to ask again.
Nunca tenha medo de perguntar de novo.

s: Charades is a party game in which a player acts out a word or a phrase without speaking, and the others have to guess.
Charadas (charades) é um jogo de festa em que um jogador representa uma palavra ou frase sem falar, e os outros precisam adivinhar.
The game is popular at birthdays and family meetings, and it makes people laugh.
O jogo é popular em aniversários e reuniões de família e faz as pessoas rirem.
When you do not understand a gesture, you ask for clarification.
Quando você não entende um gesto, pede esclarecimento.
Useful questions: “What did you say?”, “What did you mean?” and “Is it a person or a thing?”
Perguntas úteis: “What did you say?”, “What did you mean?” e “Is it a person or a thing?”
To check your guess, say “Do you mean the ogre?” or “Is it a dragon?”
Para conferir seu palpite, diga “Do you mean the ogre?” ou “Is it a dragon?”
To answer, say “Yes, you're right” or “No, try again.”
Para responder, diga “Yes, you're right” ou “No, try again.”
Gestures help when words are missing.
Gestos ajudam quando faltam palavras.

fr.title: Conheça a obra: The Once and Future King
s: “The Once and Future King” is a 1958 novel by T. H. White, which retells the legend of King Arthur.
“The Once and Future King” é um romance de 1958 de T. H. White, que reconta a lenda do rei Arthur.
The young Arthur, called Wart, is educated by the wizard Merlin, who turns him into animals to teach him about life.
O jovem Arthur, chamado Wart, é educado pelo mago Merlin, que o transforma em animais para ensinar sobre a vida.
Merlin wants to pass on his knowledge, so that the future king will rule with wisdom.
Merlin quer passar adiante seu conhecimento, para que o futuro rei governe com sabedoria.
“Pass on” means to give information or a thing to another person: “Please pass on the message.”
“Pass on” significa dar uma informação ou coisa a outra pessoa: “Please pass on the message.”
“Pass out” means to faint: “She passed out in the heat.”
“Pass out” significa desmaiar: “She passed out in the heat.”
“Pass away” is a gentle way of saying “die”.
“Pass away” é uma forma delicada de dizer “morrer”.
Pass it on, and don't pass out.
Passe adiante e não desmaie.

s: “The Story of My Life” is the 1903 autobiography of Helen Keller, who became deaf and blind as a baby and learned to communicate with the help of her teacher, Anne Sullivan.
“A História da Minha Vida” é a autobiografia de 1903 de Helen Keller, que ficou surda e cega quando bebê e aprendeu a se comunicar com a ajuda da professora, Anne Sullivan.
She wrote the book while she was still a student at Radcliffe College.
Ela escreveu o livro ainda estudante no Radcliffe College.
Her story has passed from generation to generation.
A história dela passou de geração em geração.
“Pass by” means to go near without stopping: “We passed by the house.”
“Pass by” significa passar perto sem parar: “We passed by the house.”
“Pass over” means to ignore or skip: “They passed over the mistake.”
“Pass over” significa ignorar ou pular: “They passed over the mistake.”
“Pass for” means to be accepted as something: “He could pass for a teacher.”
“Pass for” significa ser aceito como algo: “He could pass for a teacher.”
“Pass away” means to die, and “pass on” can mean the same.
“Pass away” significa morrer, e “pass on” pode significar o mesmo.

Jane, an orphan who becomes a governess, goes to work at Thornfield Hall, where she meets the mysterious Mr. Rochester.

The house hides a secret that Jane discovers on her wedding day.

Defining relative clauses identify a person or thing: “Jane is the governess who works at Thornfield.”
Orações relativas definidoras identificam uma pessoa ou coisa: “Jane is the governess who works at Thornfield.”
Use “who” for people, “which” or “that” for things, and “whose” for possession: “the man whose house is large.”

fr.title: Conheça a obra: Ebony and Ivory
s: “Ebony and Ivory” is a 1982 song by Paul McCartney and Stevie Wonder, about black and white piano keys that live together in harmony.
“Ebony and Ivory” é uma canção de 1982 de Paul McCartney e Stevie Wonder, sobre as teclas pretas e brancas do piano que convivem em harmonia.
The singers use the keys as a symbol of different people who can live together.
Os cantores usam as teclas como símbolo de pessoas diferentes que podem viver juntas.
Contrast is the main idea of the song, so it is a good example for linking opposite ideas.
O contraste é a ideia central da canção, então é um bom exemplo para ligar ideias opostas.
Use “on the other hand” to introduce a different point: “The black keys are quiet; on the other hand, the white keys are bright.”
Use “on the other hand” para introduzir outro ponto: “The black keys are quiet; on the other hand, the white keys are bright.”
Use “whereas” and “while” inside a sentence, and “in contrast” at the start.
Use “whereas” e “while” dentro da frase, e “in contrast” no começo.
“Unlike” is followed by a noun: “Unlike a guitar, a piano has keys.”
“Unlike” é seguido de um substantivo: “Unlike a guitar, a piano has keys.”
Two different sides can make one harmony.
Dois lados diferentes podem fazer uma harmonia.
